correctness.rationale: For connected triangle/C4-free G and distinct centers, closed balls B(u) are distinct and pair intersections have at most two elements. Consequently after root positive x, any second query has its positive branch of size <=2, prohibiting complete online depth 4. The root positive child can shatter depth2 exactly when degree(x)>=3 (use neighbor y, yielding two positive and at least two negative centers); root negative child depth2 iff some y satisfies 2 <= |B(y)\B(x)| <= |V\B(x)|-2, since different centers distinguishable. This gives iff Ldim=3 else 2 for n>=5. VCdim<=2 via common-neighbor obstruction to three shattered query vertices, and >=2 by neighbor witnesses for branching, paths and cycles. Eight-leaf capacity forces n>=8, explicit eight-vertex tree has depth3. Independently enumerated the 35 connected triangle/C4-free graph atlas examples through seven vertices and verified exact Ldim equals criterion; also independently checked eight-tree. Finite checks do not prove universal theorem.
